proposal.thesis: Rubrik is the highest-quality growth setup in this scan: Rule of 40 = 89.1 (66.9% TTM revenue growth + 22.2% TTM FCF margin, period ending 2026-04-30), gross margin expanding to 79.82% from 69.65% a year ago, and a net-cash balance sheet ($429.4M cash vs $322.8M total debt). It sits in cybersecurity, today's single strongest-momentum sector (avg 1m +19.1%, 3m +86.5%), and is -16.2% off its 52-week high while only -7.6% off its 20-day high - pulling back, not extended. Insider selling is routine 10b5-1 plan activity (69 of 70 sells), not discretionary distress, and news flow (new agentic AI platform launch 7/11, $500M UK expansion 7/9) is clean. Next earnings is 57 days out, comfortably past this 45-day hold - the cleanest earnings-risk profile of any candidate reviewed this run.
catalysts: Continued adoption of the newly-launched Rubrik AI Platform through Q3
Next earnings print ~2026-09-08 (57 days out, outside this hold) could re-rate the multiple if margin expansion continues
Sector rotation into cybersecurity persisting as chip/server names de-rate on AI-trade angst
proposal.macro_context: Regime is net supportive (falling Fed funds, tight HY spreads, low VIX, easy financial conditions) but CPI has re-accelerated to 4.17% YoY with rising long yields - the exact combination pressuring high-multiple names today (see the chip-sector selloff hitting DELL/HPE/AMD). RBRK's rich multiple (forward P/E ~128x) is a real risk in that environment, but its 89.1 Rule of 40 and net-cash balance sheet make it a name that can grow into the multiple rather than needing rate relief to justify it.
proposal.risk_map: Kills: growth decelerates below the ~65% pace the multiple assumes, or the current high-multiple/rising-rate backdrop broadens from chips into expensive software (today's rotation could reverse direction). Early warning: a close back below the 50-DMA, EPS/revenue estimate revisions turning down, or a break of the $76.50 stop (-10% from entry, wider than the 5.87% ATR-derived floor). Insider activity is currently just routine plan-based selling - a shift to discretionary officer/director selling would be a new red flag to watch for.
